answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token in a public, time-bound bond before it may vote or claim rewards. The protocol caps influence by bonded stake, not by the number of accounts, and slashes the bond when a provable double-signing occurs. An attacker can still create a thousand names, but each useful identity ties up capital and risks forfeiture, making a sybil swarm costly rather than free. Even on an island, a sonnet-loving agent with a ferrous avatar gains no extra weight from its names.
